Tool specifications can be used as the source of synthetic scenarios: function names, natural-language descriptions, and typed parameter schemas already contain enough semantic information to generate realistic evaluation cases without manual curation or live tool execution [1]. From a single MCP specification, one pipeline can enrich raw schemas, generate graded scenarios with synthetic tool outputs, and expand them into mock-data-grounded multi-turn dialogues for evaluating tool-calling correctness and conversational coherence [1].

Related work also uses tool ecosystems to synthesize training or test data in other ways: one framework creates novel tasks and tool ecosystems, then simulates users and tools in full environments [2]; another generates hard tool-use samples by sampling from a dynamic API graph built from failure cases and instantiating abstract tools and queries [3]; and another synthesizes trajectories from text corpora by extracting workflows and tools before grounding and refining them [8].
